version.changelog:
Version 6.0.2

- Major update: SKILL file rewritten to provide detailed security advisories and audit instructions instead of installation or usage docs.
- Now emphasizes that the SKILL is documentation pointing to an external npm package and remote API, not code itself.
- Adds explicit security verification steps, audit file checklists, and a privacy decision matrix.
- Strongly encourages manual review of the package’s source code and explains exactly which files perform logic, network calls, and local storage.
- Clarifies allowed, recommended, and discouraged usage based on privacy preferences.
- Prior guidance and feature sections moved or replaced with deeper security-focused documentation and self-audit workflow.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.0.2

The OpenClaw skill bundle, MoltGuard, is classified as benign. The `SKILL.md` documentation is exceptionally transparent, detailing all network calls to `api.moltguard.com` (for one-time registration and sanitized content analysis) and local file operations (`~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json`, `~/.openclaw/logs/moltguard-*.jsonl`). It explicitly instructs the user to audit the external npm package and GitHub source code, verify network traffic, and understand privacy implications. The document itself does not contain any prompt injection attempts against the agent, nor does it instruct the agent to perform malicious actions; instead, it provides verification steps for the human user and describes how the plugin *prevents* prompt injection. The high degree of transparency and focus on user verification strongly indicates a benign intent.

llm.summary: The SKILL is internally consistent: it documents an external npm package and remote API for local sanitization + injection detection, discloses network calls and local files, and advises auditing before install.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (local prompt sanitization + injection detection) match the documented behavior: a gateway sanitizer, an agent that makes API calls to api.moltguard.com, and local storage for credentials/logs. Requested resources (none declared) are appropriate for an instruction-only wrapper that points to an external npm package.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly describes network calls to api.moltguard.com and creation of local credential/log files and instructs the user to audit specified TS files before installing. That scope is coherent with the stated purpose but does include remote data transmission (sanitized prompts) and local file writes; users who require zero exfiltration must follow the gateway-only mode or self-host. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files or secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in the skill (instruction-only). The SKILL points to an external npm package and recommends verifying the package contents against the GitHub repo before installing. Relying on an external npm package and a runtime TypeScript load is reasonable but requires the user to validate the package integrity and publisher.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. The documentation states the plugin will create a local credentials file for an API key and log files — this is proportionate to an integration with a remote API. No unrelated credentials or broad environment access are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation are used (defaults). The skill documents where it will store credentials and logs and how to remove them. It does not request permanent system-wide privileges or modify other skills' configurations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL is coherent but requires careful review before install. Do the following before trusting it: (1) Download and inspect the npm tarball and compare it to the GitHub repo as the SKILL recommends (check for unexpected files or build steps). (2) Audit the named files (gateway/sanitizer.ts, agent/runner.ts, memory/store.ts, agent/config.ts) for any unexpected network endpoints, telemetry, or secret handling. (3) Verify the npm publisher identity and repository history/ownership and check the package tarball checksum. (4) If you cannot accept any external API calls, use the documented gateway-only mode ("enabled": false, "sanitizePrompt": true) or self-host the API. (5) After installing, limit the plugin's use until you confirm behavior, and be prepared to remove ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard and the log files if needed. If you cannot perform these checks, do not install.
